catalog_quote: 2.3 Tone and stress Chantyal is the only Tamangic language which is not tonal. Most likely, the massive influx of Nepali vocabulary contributed to the loss of the tonal system. In native vocabulary, primary stress is on the first syllable. In borrowed Nepali vocabulary, stress follows Nepali stress rules.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (48 KB scanned text of Routledge 2003 ch. 19 'Chantyal', Michael Noonan). Lines 180-187 read exactly: "2.3 Tone and stress / Chantyal is the only Tamangic language which is not tonal. Most likely, the massive influx of Nepali vocabulary contributed to the loss of the tonal system. / In native vocabulary, primary stress is on the first syllable. In borrowed Nepali vocabulary, stress follows Nepali stress rules." The passage sits between the running heads 'CHANTYAL 317' (line 139) and '318 THE SINO-TIBETAN LANGUAGES' (line 221), so p. 317 is correct; it is followed by 2.4 Phonotactics, and section 2.1 (p. 316, line 77-80) adds the stressed/unstressed allophony of /ə/ as the compiler no…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Chantyal has no tone (unlike every other Tamangic language). Primary stress falls on the first syllable of native words; Nepali loanwords keep the stress placement of Nepali (i.e. a separate, borrowed stratum with its own rules).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned; only 'primary stress' is named.
new_statements.exceptions: Borrowed Nepali vocabulary (a large part of the lexicon) follows Nepali stress rules rather than initial stress; the vowel section also notes /ə/ is realized differently when stressed vs unstressed (allophony, p. 316).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement ('in native vocabulary'); no discussion of phrase-level prominence or citation forms. Speech of Mangale Khani village is the variety represented (p. 315).
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Chantyal as spoken in the eastern Myagdi District villages, specifically the speech of Mangale Khani (Noonan 2003: 315); the Baglung Chantyal no longer speak the language. This is the language-level chan1310 (ISO chx); no separate dialect glottocode involved.
